title: Arriving in El Paso: Tiny Joe, George Alexander and the California nightclub
summary: Watts reaches El Paso, works four or five months with a band, and describes the booker Tiny Joe and George Alexander's California club, where tips equalled salary and fights broke out beside the bar.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We got the reel three Bob Watson, it's February this time. February the 28th, 1963 and we were getting to El Paso and you would have sent them a telegram there.

Yeah. Well, Guy Moe, they sent it, as I said before, a couple of days, two or three days they sent me what I asked for so I went on up there, see, and then I played, oh I must have worked with them about four or five months, see. I worked there with them about four or five months. And then I don't know, I got to the place where I just wanted to get up a little group of my own, you know. I got in touch with some fellas there, see. Tiny Joe, that was a booker, a very, about 350 pound colored fella. Yeah. But he was a kind man, a booker, or anything else, man, see, that you could say bad about him. I've heard about him, I haven't seen it. He done fooled some boys in El Paso to play at the California nightclub, that's Alfred Williams' old stomping ground, from Mr. George Alexander. He done fooled some boys, he come away from Waco out here, man, oh man, I guarantee you forty dollars a week. You just come on out here, I've got to work for you. But when the boys come out here, Tiny Joe ain't had nothing for him. And they was stranded at the California. But George wasn't open? Yeah, George, for George Alexander, I said. Well, he was open, was he running his nightclub then?
Yeah, yeah, yeah. But he didn't have the job, eh? Did he have the job for the boys? Oh yeah. He had it.

Yeah, Tiny Joe did. But how long did it last? Well, it lasted a long time, see, but they didn't have no trumpet man. Oh. You see? They come out here, they had piano, drums, banjo, and drums, and sax, see. And I done went down there a couple of times, you know, and heard them rehearsing evening, see, and they fit, you know, I could fit right in with them, see, and they didn't have heard me blowing. They wanted me, see, but they had been putting a little pressure on me, but I didn't want to put Guy down, because he was the cause of me, he pulled me out of a hole, you know, because Guy was making a lot down there, man. Guy's tip was as much as your salary, my salary was there for George, I'm going to tell you the truth. That's right. Just the tips in that district joint, see. That's what I mean. But I don't know, I just, too much went on down there, man. Them people, man, the laws was running around there all the time, man. If it wasn't the women fighting, it wasn't them men fighting, you know, see, man, you know. They might get killed. Yeah, you know, see, man, because quite a couple of times I had to jump behind the piano, you understand, see, drawing them guns, you know. Right close to the bar. You understand, see. Right at the International Bridge, just about two blocks. Yeah, see. And so I was always nervous, so I could feel myself, man, just getting to be a nervous wreck.
I know I was too young for that. That was in 34 or 35. Yeah, around that time. Yeah, because it was open in 36 when I got out there. Yeah, yeah. And you had been out there, you see.

Oh yeah, oh yeah. 34. That's right, that's right. Yeah, that's what George told me. Yeah. And then I went in the, see, then I quit them. Oh, I let them know that I was going. They didn't care, because they was making a lot of money, but God said he wished I would stick.
